items.claim: Every Masoretic fact this row asserts holds on the witness. MT 26:15 opens a messenger formula addressed to Tyre; the mark record carries a setumah after MT 26:18 and a setumah after MT 26:21 and nothing else inside the span, and the row discloses both. MT 26:19 renews the messenger formula (כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה) while the addressee stays second-person feminine (בְּתִתִּ֤י אֹתָךְ֙), so the row is right that no addressee change accompanies the mark at MT 26:18. The span carries no ketiv/qere site and no editorial note, as the row states, and the two paseq occurrences of MT 26 stand at MT 26:15 and MT 26:16, both inside the span and both taken as counts only. Across all six rows of this cluster every reference the row does carry as boundary evidence lies inside its own span and every flagged one lies outside it, so the flags track cross-span neighbour and comparison citation, not a missing ground.
items.both_sides: At the seam behind the row, MT 26:14 closes with the spoken clause that reads the divine name and the utterance signature and is followed by a setumah, while MT 26:15 opens a fresh messenger formula; both sides agree on a cut there. At the internal seam MT 26:18/26:19 the sides disagree: the mark layer shows a setumah after MT 26:18, but MT 26:18 itself closes with no recognition, no utterance and no spoken-clause formula, and MT 26:19 reopens the same addressee, so the text layer withholds the cut the mark layer would allow. At the row's close MT 26:21 the sides agree again: the utterance signature ends the verse and a setumah follows, and MT 27:1 begins a new word-event opening.

Second, the lament noun recurs inside the span at MT 27:32 (וְנָשְׂא֨וּ אֵלַ֤יִךְ בְּנִיהֶם֙ קִינָ֔ה וְקוֹנְנ֖וּ), in the same reported-speech shape the row contrasts its opening command with at MT 26:17 (וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙), which lies outside the span, while the in-span instance goes unmentioned. A third ground the row gives against internal cuts at MT 27:11/27:12 and at MT 27:25/27:26 is a poetic-line layout feature rather than a textual one; the checkable grounds at those two points are that the mark record carries nothing there and no formula stands in either verse, and both of those are true. Across all six rows of this cluster every reference the row does carry as boundary evidence lies inside its own span and every flagged one lies outside it, so the flags track cross-span neighbour and comparison citation, not a missing ground.
items.both_sides: Behind the row, MT 26:21 closes on the utterance signature with a setumah following, and MT 27:1 opens a full word-event onset, so both sides agree on the cut at MT 26:21/27:1. Ahead, MT 27:36 closes with no recognition, no utterance and no spoken-clause formula in the verse, and the mark record carries a setumah after it, so the close rests on the mark plus the verse's own terminal clause; MT 28:1 then opens a full word-event onset, which corroborates the cut from the far side. On the whole-chapter question the Masoretic layer supports the row: MT 27 carries exactly one parashah mark, the setumah after its last verse, and no internal mark at all, so nothing in that layer argues for an internal seam even though the span runs far past the size guidance.

items.claim: The row says the terminal clause at MT 28:19 mirrors the one at MT 27:36 exactly. On the pointed bytes it does not. MT 27:36 reads בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד עוֹלָֽם, with second-person feminine forms for the city, and MT 28:19 reads בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם, with second-person masculine forms for the king; the verb and the negated existential with its suffix both differ. The two agree only once the pointing is stripped, so the claim of exact identity conflates a pointed collation with an accent-stripped one, and it erases a contrast that is itself boundary evidence, since the shift from the feminine city addressee to the masculine king addressee is part of what separates this row from the one before it. The row's other Masoretic facts hold: the mark after MT 28:19 is a petuchah, correctly typed and not equated with a setumah, MT 28:19 carries no recognition, no utterance and no spoken-clause formula, and the span carries no ketiv/qere site and no editorial note. Across all six rows of this cluster every reference the row does carry as boundary evidence lies inside its own span and every flagged one lies outside it, so the flags track cross-span neighbour and comparison citation, not a missing ground.
items.both_sides: Behind the row, MT 28:10 closes on a spoken clause plus the utterance signature with a setumah following, and MT 28:11 opens a full word-event onset followed at MT 28:12 by its own lament command naming the king; both sides agree on the cut. Ahead, the sides are unequal: MT 28:19 carries no close formula at all, so the close rests on the petuchah plus the verse's own terminal clause, while MT 28:20 opens a full word-event onset and MT 28:21 turns the face toward a new addressee. The far side therefore carries the cut, and correcting the mirror claim leaves it standing.

items.claim: This two-verse row rests its distinct justification on a precedent it describes as a formula-bounded unit under three verses with a messenger onset, a recognition close and a parashah mark, at MT 33:21-22. Only the mark is there. MT 33:21 opens וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ — a dated notice followed by the fugitive's report — and carries no messenger formula; MT 33:22 reads וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י, narrative about the prophet's mouth, and carries no recognition formula. The setumah after MT 33:22 is the one described feature the record confirms. The row's own boundary evidence is sound and independent of the precedent: the messenger formula at MT 28:25 (כֹּֽה אָמַר֮), the paseq occurrence recorded there, the full recognition close at MT 28:26 (מִסְּבִ֣יבוֹתָ֔ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם) and the setumah after it, with no ketiv/qere site and no editorial note in the span. Across all six rows of this cluster every reference the row does carry as boundary evidence lies inside its own span and every flagged one lies outside it, so the flags track cross-span neighbour and comparison citation, not a missing ground. The flagged comparison at MT 33:21-22 is the one that fails on the bytes.
items.both_sides: Behind the row, both sides support the cut at MT 28:24/28:25 but neither is decisive alone: MT 28:24 carries a recognition close and a setumah after it, yet the addressee turn toward Israel starts inside MT 28:24 rather than after it, while MT 28:25 supplies the fresh messenger formula that opens a bounded speech unit. Ahead, the sides agree: MT 28:26 ends on the fullest form of the recognition formula with a setumah after it, and MT 29:1 opens on a dated notice (MT 29:1, outside the numbering zone, so MT and WEB agree there) rather than continuing the speech. The precedent correction does not touch either side.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Read-form rendering, instances only, not adjudicated. Four ketiv/qere sites fall in this cluster: MT 27:3, MT 27:6, MT 27:15 and MT 28:3. The running Masoretic text carries only the written form at each - הישבתי at MT 27:3, כתים at MT 27:6, והובנים at MT 27:15 and מדנאל at MT 28:3 - and the read form occurs nowhere in that running text. At MT 27:3, MT 27:15 and MT 28:3 the mark record holds the read form with the source's morpheme separator and the rows render it with the separator removed; at MT 27:6 the record holds no separator and the row's rendering agrees with the record. The rows disclose the removal in words. The non-witness strings are deliberately not reproduced here.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Whether this rendering is a sanctioned corpus convention decides whether four evidence lines in this cluster quote a string the witness does not contain. It is recorded as data for the ruling already in progress and is not judged here.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Scope of the comma-placed-denial rule. It was applied here to denials about puncta and about datelines, and this cluster carries neither. One denial of a different kind does sit behind a comma, in the evidence label for MT 26:19, which denies an addressee-class shift in that position.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the rule reaches any denial rather than puncta and dateline denials only, that one label needs rewording and the verdict on the row covering MT 26:15-MT 26:21 would move from support to challenge on wording grounds, with none of its Masoretic facts affected.

The Masoretic layer gives no internal seam at all, so this lens can only report that nothing in the mark or formula record argues for a cut; whether the span is nonetheless too long is a question for the form lens and the size guidance, not for the bytes.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The row is held at a reduced confidence for its length; the original-language evidence neither raises nor lowers that, and saying so keeps the two lenses from being read as one.
